title: 2011 HMMT February Calculus and Combinatorics Problem 2
statement: Let \(a, b\), and \(c\) be positive real numbers. Determine the largest total number of real roots that the following three polynomials may have among them: \(a x^{2}+b x+c, b x^{2}+c x+a\), and \(c x^{2}+a x+b\).

solutions.text: 4 If all the polynomials had real roots, their discriminants would all be nonnegative: \(a^{2} \geq\) \(4 b c, b^{2} \geq 4 c a\), and \(c^{2} \geq 4 a b\). Multiplying these inequalities gives \((a b c)^{2} \geq 64(a b c)^{2}\), a contradiction. Hence one of the quadratics has no real roots. The maximum of 4 real roots is attainable: for example, the values \((a, b, c)=(1,5,6)\) give \(-2,-3\) as roots to \(x^{2}+5 x+6\) and \(-1,-\frac{1}{5}\) as roots to \(5 x^{2}+6 x+1\).
